draft.title: Entitlements and transition
card: Entitlements are what a departing employee is owed by law or by their contract. They include unpaid wages and accrued (built up) annual leave that has not been taken.
Long service leave may also be owed, depending on how long the person worked for the business and the rules that apply to them.

Redundancy pay is owed only in some cases. It is paid when the job no longer exists, and the amount usually depends on how long the person has worked there. It is not paid when an employee simply resigns.
Transition support helps the person move on. Outplacement is one example: the business pays for services such as résumé writing, interview coaching and job search help.
draft.remember: Entitlements are what the employee is owed. Transition support is extra help to find the next job.

a.q: Which of these is an example of transition support for a departing employee?
opts: A business pays a career coach to help a worker find a job
A business pays out annual leave the worker has not taken
A business pays the final week of wages that is still owed
A business pays redundancy pay based on years of service
a.why: A career coach helps the person find new work, which is outplacement, a form of transition support. The other three are payments the person is owed, so they are entitlements. Redundancy pay is tempting, but it is money owed, not help with moving on.
a.clue: Which option helps the person find work rather than paying money owed?

b.q: Priya resigns from her job at a Geelong bakery to start her own business. She has two weeks of unpaid wages and some unused annual leave. What is the business required to pay her?
opts: The unpaid wages and the accrued annual leave
The unpaid wages only, as leave is lost on resigning
The unpaid wages and leave, plus redundancy pay
Nothing, because she chose to leave the business
b.why: Unpaid wages and accrued annual leave are owed whenever an employee leaves, including when they resign. Redundancy pay is only owed when the job no longer exists, and Priya's job still does. The idea that leaving by choice cancels what is owed is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: Redundancy pay depends on the job ending. Wages and leave do not.

a.best: A business pays a career coach to help a worker find a job

b.best: The unpaid wages and the accrued annual leave
